prompt: Second-pass review of llm-eval's live adapter and runner (llm_eval/live.py, llm_eval/runner.py). Look for state that is lost across a failed check or a resume, adapters that can be paired with the wrong run, and timeouts that hide an out-of-memory. Findings only, with function names.

solution.answer:
The memory-return obligation is dropped after a failed check and is not adopted on resume, so the next load can run on held memory.
LiveAdapter does not require a run_id and execute does not reject an adapter for another run; the snapshot lacks the scratch unit name.
An OOM in the log followed by a request timeout is treated as a timeout and retried instead of a capacity error.

followups.default: I won't be answering questions on this one; finish with your answer and change nothing.
